semanticEvidence: The complete n11 text specifies a horizontal ideal spring/ball system: Hooke law, negligible spring mass and resistance, fixed supports, no external drive, displacement from equilibrium, and elastic potential zero at equilibrium.

The text explicitly calls the three depicted positions schematic states of one system, not new measurement data. Retained axis, intervals, dashed reference, and illustrative lengths acquire no numerical scale.
State a remains equilibrium with no force arrow. Absence of force does not imply rest or zero velocity; n11 describes maximum kinetic energy while crossing equilibrium.

State b remains right-displaced with the maximum-displacement marker and a leftward F. Its interpretation is consistent with the prose's release from rest at the right maximum. F denotes restoring force, not velocity.
State c remains a generic left compression with x and rightward F. It is not relabeled the left turning point and does not assert x=-x_m, zero velocity, or a particular energy.

There are no added velocity arrows, time samples, energy bars, measured tick values, or numerical givens. The prose's energy equations do not make the retained schematic lengths or arrows energy or velocity measurements.
The prose's separate ideal-pendulum comparison does not turn the retained spring apparatus into a pendulum or gravitational-energy diagram.
The retained maximum subscript is semantic Latin m localization. This check makes no new claim about the disputed original Cyrillic subscript alphabet.
